trl_rationale: The topic names a product (tandem solar cells and modules), so the process-scope discount does not apply. Market sources confirm two named companies with commercial products of the topic's own system. Oxford PV made a first commercial deployment of 72-cell, 24.5%-efficient tandem modules for a utility-scale installation (M7, M2). Trina Solar announced a first commercial order for tandem modules deployed in New Zealand (M1). Trina also reported a TÜV SÜD-certified 29.2%, 907 W full-size 3.1 m² module (M1). Academic sources add independently certified 29.15% to 32.73% monolithic cells and stability in the thousands of hours (A5, A3, A1). Together these place the technology past TRL 7 with early TRL 8 signals. The score stops short of TRL 8 because deployment volumes are described as selective, the customers are unnamed, and the registry contains no reliability-qualification, damp-heat or outdoor field data. Lab stability tops out at roughly 1,000–2,200 h, with 88% retained after 1,000 h at 65 °C (A1, A3).
mrl_rationale: Manufacturing evidence shows pilot-to-early-commercial production rather than validated low-rate production. Oxford PV produces its cells on a megawatt-scale pilot line in Brandenburg, began delivering to module partners in 2024, and is still searching for a gigawatt-scale site (M7, M5). LONGi and CubicPV describe pilot lines in China and the U.S. rather than volume production (M4). Trina's certified industrial-size module and first order show production-representative capability but no disclosed volume (M1). No source reports yield, throughput, capacity or cost-per-watt data, and the sources conflict on Oxford PV's production start date (M4, M5). Academic sources still flag wide-bandgap film homogeneity and crystallization control as an unresolved reproducibility challenge (A1, A6), although ambient-air processing on HJT bottom cells points toward manufacturability (A3).
evidence_rationale: All three domains are covered. The academic sources are peer-reviewed journal records, including four foundational Science papers with more than 2,000 citations each (A5, A6, A7, A8). However, A7 and A8 concern single-junction cells, the 2026 papers have 0–1 citations, and A4 is a low-credibility deposit excluded from conclusions. The patent evidence consists of search snippets from a single aggregator with unverified legal status (P1–P8). All market sources are medium-credibility trade news, unverified company-style content or commercial estimates (M1–M8). They also contain an unresolved timeline conflict (M4 vs. M5) and widely divergent forecasts. Material gaps remain in field durability, yield and cost data, which keeps confidence at good rather than strong.
scoring_rationale:
Perovskite-silicon tandems sit in the pilot-to-early-commercial band. Two named manufacturers have made first commercial deployments: Oxford PV for utility-scale (M7) and Trina for premium residential (M1). Trina has also certified a full-size 29.2% module (M1). Lab cells reach 32.73% certified efficiency (A3).

Manufacturing remains at megawatt-scale pilot lines with no yield or cost data (M7, M5, M4). Durability evidence is limited to lab tests in the thousands of hours (A1, A3). Together these cap MRL and keep TRL below full qualification.

The patent landscape is filling quickly, with core architectures and textured-silicon deposition represented (P1, P2, P6, P7). Market formation is real but small and poorly quantified (M3, M6, M8). Evidence spans all three domains but relies on medium-credibility market sources and patent snippets.
key_risks: Long-term durability is unproven. The best reported stability is 88% retained after 1,000 h at 65 °C (A1) and a T80 of 2,182 h unencapsulated (A3). No field, damp-heat or certification-standard reliability data appear in the registry, and M6 flags durability as a key readiness question. This threatens bankability for utility buyers.

Large Chinese silicon incumbents report record tandem cells and pilot roadmaps (M2, M4) and benefit from Asia-Pacific's dominant manufacturing share (M3, M8). This creates strong competitive pressure on smaller or Western entrants.

Manufacturing scale-up is unresolved. Oxford PV is still searching for a gigawatt-scale site (M5, M7). Wide-bandgap film crystallization and phase homogeneity remain a yield and reproducibility challenge (A1, A6).

Core tandem concepts are already represented in patent filings: monolithic 2T interconnection (P1, P6), textured-silicon deposition (P2, P7) and module overlay integration (P4, P8). A claims-level freedom-to-operate review is needed before product development.
Market sizing is highly uncertain. 2026 estimates diverge about 12×, and they cover broad perovskite rather than tandem-only revenue (M3, M6, M8).
key_opportunities: Premium residential, rooftop and specialty segments are emerging as early paid markets where per-area efficiency justifies a price premium (M1, M6, M7). These segments offer entry points that avoid head-on competition in commodity utility volume.

Gigawatt-scale tandem manufacturing capacity outside China, and the equipment and partnering to support it, appears underserved (M5, M7, M4). This creates openings for equipment vendors, contract manufacturers and module partners.

Independent reliability testing, warranty and field-monitoring services could gain traction because current commercial evidence centres on efficiency certifications rather than durability (M1, M5, M6).

Interface engineering with self-assembled monolayers and ambient-air processing on HJT bottom cells is becoming a design platform (A3, A5). This could make SAM materials and interface know-how strategically valuable.

Within the retrieved sample, lead-free top cells on textured crystalline wafers, lifecycle recycling and in-line metrology appear underrepresented (P5, P2, P7, P8). These are preliminary observations that require comprehensive search and claims review by patent counsel.

market_comparison.limitation: Same-definition market estimates were not verified. The legacy amount-spread flag does not establish currency, metric, year, geography, scope or method comparability. Its amounts are not verified USD estimates. Neither an absent flag nor a score at 3.5 proves agreement or an actual deduction.
